question: Can you provide the top 9 directors by movie count, including their ID, name, number of movies, average inter-movie duration (rounded to the nearest integer), average rating (rounded to 2 decimals), total votes, minimum and maximum ratings, and total movie duration? Sort the output first by movie count in descending order and then by total movie duration in descending order.
sql:
WITH ordered_movies AS (
    SELECT 
        dm.name_id,
        n.name,
        m.id as movie_id,
        m.date_published,
        m.duration,
        r.avg_rating,
        r.total_votes,
        LAG(m.date_published) OVER (PARTITION BY dm.name_id ORDER BY m.date_published) as prev_date
    FROM director_mapping dm
    JOIN names n ON dm.name_id = n.id
    JOIN movies m ON dm.movie_id = m.id
    JOIN ratings r ON m.id = r.movie_id
),
inter_duration AS (
    SELECT 
        name_id,
        name,
        duration,
        avg_rating,
        total_votes,
        prev_date,
        CASE 
            WHEN prev_date IS NOT NULL THEN 
                ROUND(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (date_published - prev_date)) / 86400.0)
            ELSE NULL
        END as days_between_movies
    FROM ordered_movies
),
director_stats AS (
    SELECT 
        name_id,
        name,
        COUNT(*) as movie_count,
        SUM(duration) as total_movie_duration,
        ROUND(AVG(avg_rating), 2) as avg_rating,
        SUM(total_votes) as total_votes,
        MIN(avg_rating) as min_rating,
        MAX(avg_rating) as max_rating
    FROM inter_duration
    GROUP BY name_id, name
),
director_inter_duration AS (
    SELECT 
        name_id,
        ROUND(AVG(days_between_movies)) as avg_inter_movie_duration
    FROM inter_duration
    GROUP BY name_id
)
SELECT 
    ds.name_id,
    ds.name,
    ds.movie_count,
    COALESCE(did.avg_inter_movie_duration, 0) as avg_inter_movie_duration,
    ds.avg_rating,
    ds.total_votes,
    ds.min_rating,
    ds.max_rating,
    ds.total_movie_duration
FROM director_stats ds
LEFT JOIN director_inter_duration did ON ds.name_id = did.name_id
ORDER BY ds.movie_count DESC, ds.total_movie_duration DESC
LIMIT 9

WITH director_movies AS (
    SELECT 
        dm.name_id,
        n.name,
        m.id as movie_id,
        m.date_published,
        m.duration as movie_duration,
        r.avg_rating,
        r.total_votes,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY dm.name_id ORDER BY m.date_published) as rn
    FROM director_mapping dm
    JOIN names n ON dm.name_id = n.id
    JOIN movies m ON dm.movie_id = m.id
    JOIN ratings r ON m.id = r.movie_id
),
director_stats AS (
    SELECT 
        name_id,
        name,
        COUNT(*) as movie_count,
        ROUND(AVG(m.duration)) as total_duration,
        ROUND(AVG(avg_rating), 2) as avg_rating,
        SUM(total_votes) as total_votes,
        MIN(avg_rating) as min_rating,
        MAX(avg_rating) as max_rating
    FROM director_movies
    GROUP BY name_id, name
),
inter_movie_duration AS (
    SELECT 
        dm.name_id,
        dm.name,
        AVG(
            CASE 
                WHEN dm.rn > 1 THEN 
                    (julianday(dm.date_published) - julianday(
                        LAG(dm.date_published) OVER (PARTITION BY dm.name_id ORDER BY dm.rn)
                    )) * 365.25
                ELSE NULL
            END
        ) as avg_inter_movie_duration
    FROM director_movies dm
    GROUP BY dm.name_id, dm.name
)
SELECT 
    ds.name_id,
    ds.name,
    ds.movie_count,
    ROUND(COALESCE(imd.avg_inter_movie_duration, 0)) as avg_inter_movie_duration,
    ds.avg_rating,
    ds.total_votes,
    ds.min_rating,
    ds.max_rating,
    ds.total_duration
FROM director_stats ds
LEFT JOIN inter_movie_duration imd ON ds.name_id = imd.name_id
ORDER BY ds.movie_count DESC, ds.total_duration DESC
LIMIT 20
</parameter>
